name: Capstone — The Investor Dashboard
env: Power BI Desktop — the visual twin of the SQL data room. Build the four pages in Power BI; the app holds the plan, the measures, and the acceptance criteria for self-check.
goal: Turn the model and measures into a multi-page Power BI dashboard a CFO opens during a board meeting — the visual twin of the SQL data room.

brief.body: The PE firm got the SQL data room and loved it — but the board doesn't read SQL. They want to click. Build me a Power BI dashboard that tells the same story: revenue quality and growth, customer health, the funnel, and what it costs us to acquire revenue. Clean, fast, honest. If a partner clicks 'Electronics, Q3 2024,' every number should move together. This is the artifact I present.

clinic.title: Dashboard design that earns trust
clinic.body: One page = one question. Lead each page with 3–5 KPI cards (the headline), then supporting visuals below. Put slicers (Category, Year/Quarter) top or left and let them filter the whole page. Choose visuals by intent: trend → line; comparison → bar/column; part-to-whole → stacked bar (not pie); detail → matrix; funnel → funnel visual. One accent color, labelled axes, formatted ₹ and %. Add a 'data as of' note. Less chart-junk, more clarity. The four pages mirror the data room: 1) Revenue Quality & Growth · 2) Customer Health · 3) Funnel & Web · 4) Marketing & Reconciliation.

steps.instr: KPI header row — five Card visuals across the top.
steps.sql:
Cards: [Net Revenue], [Net Margin %], [Return Rate %], [Net Revenue YTD], [Net Revenue MoM %]
Format ₹ with thousands; % to one decimal.
steps.checkpoint: Five cards reading sensible values (Net Revenue ≈ ₹115 cr before slicing).

steps.sql:
Line chart: axis dim_date[YearMonth], value [Net Revenue] (+ optional [Net Revenue Running]).
Clustered column: axis dim_date[YearQuarter], value [Net Revenue], legend dim_product[Category].
steps.checkpoint: Line shows trajectory; columns show category mix per quarter. Both react to slicers.

steps.instr: The category × quarter matrix — DR-1 made interactive.
steps.sql: Matrix: rows dim_product[Category], columns dim_date[YearQuarter], values [Net Revenue] and [Net Margin %]. Subtotals on.
steps.checkpoint: The matrix matches your SQL DR-1 numbers for a spot-checked cell. If they disagree, a measure or the model is wrong — fix before continuing.

steps.sql: Slicers: dim_product[Category], dim_date[Year]/[Quarter]. Add page title + 'Data as of Dec 2024'.
steps.checkpoint: Select 'Electronics' + '2024' — every visual updates coherently. Page 1 is board-ready.

tickets.title: Page 2 — Customer Health
tickets.prompt: LTV-tier concentration, segment mix, and a customer-count trend. Cards: Distinct Customers, New Customers, top-tier revenue %. Visuals: stacked bar of revenue by Segment; a tier table; New Customers by month. Build in Power BI; self-check against the criteria.
acceptanceCriteria: Uses [Distinct Customers], [New Customers], [% of Total Revenue]
Top-tier concentration visible at a glance
Deduped — counts tie to the SQL customer scorecard (DR-2)
tickets.modelNote: Reuse the DAX-8S measures. The numbers must tie to DR-2 from the data room — if the dashboard and SQL disagree, the model relationship is wrong.

tickets.title: Page 3 — Funnel & Web
tickets.prompt: Built on fact_web_events: a Funnel visual (view → cart → checkout → purchase) and step conversion %s, plus sessions by device and by month. Call out the biggest leak. Reveal the reference DAX for the funnel measures.
acceptanceCriteria: Funnel uses distinct sessions per stage (DISTINCTCOUNT measure)
A text/callout naming the biggest drop-off step
tickets.solution:
Sessions Viewed    = CALCULATE ( DISTINCTCOUNT ( fact_web_events[session_id] ), fact_web_events[event_type]="page_view" )
Sessions Carted    = CALCULATE ( DISTINCTCOUNT ( fact_web_events[session_id] ), fact_web_events[event_type]="add_to_cart" )
Sessions Checkout  = CALCULATE ( DISTINCTCOUNT ( fact_web_events[session_id] ), fact_web_events[event_type]="checkout_start" )
Sessions Purchased = CALCULATE ( DISTINCTCOUNT ( fact_web_events[session_id] ), fact_web_events[event_type]="purchase" )
Overall Conversion % = DIVIDE ( [Sessions Purchased], [Sessions Viewed] )
tickets.modelNote: The biggest leak is view → cart (62,000 → 27,852, ~55% drop). That's the number to lead the growth conversation with.

tickets.title: Page 4 — Marketing & Reconciliation
tickets.prompt: ROAS and spend by channel/month (from DAX-802), plus a small reconciliation summary (revenue vs collected, orphans, unpaid) as KPI cards so the cash story is visible. The CFO's page.
acceptanceCriteria: Reconciliation KPIs (₹ uncollected, orphan ₹) — from the gold model or a small fact
ROAS limitation noted on the page (blended, not attributed)
tickets.modelNote: Bring the DR-4 reconciliation numbers onto a card so the cash story is one glance. Label ROAS as blended so nobody over-reads it.

finalReview.title: Final Review — the live demo
finalReview.body: 15-minute live demo to Arjun and the board. Drive the dashboard, don't read it: open on the headline, slice to the story (the growing category, the funnel leak, the concentration risk), and field 'click here / what about returns?' on the fly. The test is whether the dashboard answers follow-up questions without going back to SQL. Publish it: export to .pbix for the portfolio, optionally publish to the Power BI Service for a shareable link.
